item.content:encoded:

In other words, it's 'the greater good' theory, but in a way the reader understands the greater good on an immediate level, while also being aware of the sacrifice.

a) I think that's rather disgusting, as that's not actually how the greater good should be considered… for example the wanton sacrifice of individuals within a nation to "avoid spending 12 percent of it's GDP on imports." Not sure how dicey of a moral dilemma you've created here as its on its face, abominable.
b) this is has sorta been done alot on the wiki as well.

The 'God Eater' thing is part of the narrative. It was originally built with the intention to kill ("Eat") gods. With that in mind, it was designed to contain an entity with great power and convert it into raw unthinking energy. It just so happens that it's current users aren't aware of it's designed purpose and utilize it differently.

ok, but my point is that you need to thematically connect the anomaly to the "narrative". For example, if something broke down matter to create energy, I wouldn't assume that was used for killing gods. Typically we don't consider gods to simply be beings of matter. So what I am suggesting is you tweak this anomaly such that it is clear from the anomaly itself that there is something in it that is meant to kill the divine.

As someone fairly interesting in deicide as a narrative device, I am not sure what more you're trying to say. So the thing was meant to kill gods… ok? What thematic core to this anomaly/narrative are you trying to talk about? If its just a thing that which should kill a god… without more, I am not sure how intriguing that will be (not to mention there's plenty of that on the wiki too).

What I think you need to do is stop worrying so much about the plot and start thinking about some themes you could examine through this piece. What are you trying to talk about to the reader?

If its just "this crazy thing exists and oh isn't it a dilemma with a government using it this way" then I still have two problems:
1) the narrative does not seem connected to the anomaly. Why does it kill gods at all? Why would going into the lore of the object connect thematically to the discussion of a callous government willing to sacrifice human lives to save on annual budgets for imports?

2) As it stands, this mostly seems concerned with the discussion of the anomalous properties and the spooky implications of a callous government… but I think to stand out, it needs more. I also think the anomaly itself could be tweaked to differentiate itself from that thing that eats a life and makes energy (you can argue all you want, but why couldn't the government put in ANY organic matter to have the same effect? There's nothing inherently more potent in a human organism than others concerning the conversion of mass into energy.)

item.title: Re: Deus Comedenti (Translation: God Eater)
item.content:encoded:
1. The 'God Eater' thing is part of the narrative. It was originally built with the intention to kill ("Eat") gods. With that in mind, it was designed to contain an entity with great power and convert it into raw unthinking energy. It just so happens that it's current users aren't aware of it's designed purpose and utilize it differently.

2. The machine isn't so much *fed* by death, as it made to transform living human mass. As in once you put a human in and start the process, the mass is broken down to energy, following mass-energy equivalence (E=MC^2). It needs to be human because the runic magic (the machine is an integration of tech and runic magic) was designed to target sentient beings containing akiva, and humans *just* about hit the mark for it to function.

+ show block
– hide block

3. The 'must be stopped' is actually kinda subjective. As in, it helps a country with 1.2 billion people not only avoid spending 12 percent of it's GDP on imports (not to mention that's just the oil %age today, in a world where the oil-energy transition has progressed further, and renewable energy is the big import, it could well be higher), but also provides some income in energy export.
To put things in perspective, that's more than 120 billion dollars freed up to be spent on developing the country, infrastructure, public works (, corruption) etc.

4. I'm actually focusing on two parallel narratives:

-One being the utilization of something admittedly horrific, by a government for something extremely important in a way that the reader can figure out him/herself the importance. In other words, it's 'the greater good' theory, but in a way the reader understands the greater good on an immediate level, while also being aware of the sacrifice.

-The other, more hidden narrative, is the god eater part. I'm not going to outright 'say' the machine was intended to break down gods into pure energy, but I'm going to hint it. Like, the absolute ridiculous amount of energy the machine can store in it's battery, only about a third of which is ever actually utilised by the govt, and a big part of that's maintaining a buffer. How strong the containment circle is warded and etched with ancient runes not commonly seen in use in modern times. I'm also considering having the energy go through a 'Akiva Filter' of sorts, but that might be too obvious. The biggest hint by far, of course, is the name, for those who bother to put it in Google translate.

5. I hope that was enough to answer your bigger concerns. It's an anomaly that breaks down mass to energy (on a surface level), and has a narrative (s) built around that anomoly regarding it's use.

item.title: Re: Deus Comedenti (Translation: God Eater)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the comments.
To answer a couple of observations:

-It's in latin because it wasn't actually created in India, it just ended up there before being recovered by the foundation.

-India currently imports 5 times the value of it's exports in oil alone. That's a pretty big trade deficit. Once the transition from oil to renewable energy progresses more, the oil import would essentially be replaced with energy.With the use of the anomoly the govt avoids the deficit, even making some in "clean" energy export, but the scale of the energy requirement would probably be much higher than it is today. That said, with 400k+ in prison, probably still manageable, albeit with more casualties.

item.title: Re: Deus Comedenti (Translation: God Eater)
item.content:encoded:
1) Given that India creates about 1547 TW per year, it should take about 1623 Indian males to provide the energy India needs. Tragic, but not quite at genocidal levels. As India has a prison population of about 430K, it should be easy to make the required number disappear.

Assuming that the battery hold enough energy for India's consumption, this is actually not as bad as you estimated.

[In case you're curious, India has had 720 capital deaths since 1947. Also, given that The Foundation goes through 3K+ D-Class annually, this isn't as bad as you think.]

2) This also keeps it out of the political/targeted area. This makes essentially fodder for questioning what a government is willing to do for its people, and what those people are willing to ignore if it's to their benefit.

3) It feels weird that it has a Latin name given it's an Indian anomaly. Just sayin'.

4) Overall, it's not a bad concept and allows for some pretty good political commentary.

item.title: Deus Comedenti
item.content:encoded:
A machine that can convert mass (specifically humans) into energy. Utilized by a govt to power society, allowed mostly due to bureaucratic inertia

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Kafkaesque themes

Page Layout: It will be presented as an SCP Entry. The main narrative will be played out through the discovery logs and attached notes.

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: There is a machine called "Deus Comedenti", latin for "God Eater". It was built to kill and harvest the energy of a God, but this fact is implied rather than told outright.

The machine can also be used to harvest energy from any sentient life (on par with humans, but not animals).It comes attached with a tower-like battery with a vast storage capacity (it's built to contain the sum of a God's power) the size of a 2 story building.

Even though each individual human provides a lot of power (in terms of electricity), it takes the equivalent of a genocide of tragic proportions to fill the battery even an 1/8th of the way. It was 1/3 full as found.

Central Narrative:
Basically this is set sometime in the near future where the transition from Oil to energy is more complete. Oil is thus almost obselete, and cars and the like which used to run on oil have been adapted to use electricity.

In this setting, the Foundation finds that India has been utilising the machine to meet the vast energy demands of the country. India's current biggest import is oil, so if oil is replaced with renewable energy, it makes sense that the country would try to develop an alternative way to produce energy, so as to reduce necessary imports where energy replaces oil as the biggest import. Large solar power plants are already being built in real life in India for much the same reason.

The energy obtained from the machine is 'laundered' through the solar power plants.

The scheme was introduced as a stop gap till a better energy source could be developed, but then inertia took hold. Since not many people were aware of it at any given time, and it served the purpose well, successive govts. decided it was easier to keep using it than to develop entirely new costly energy sources.

The human input is secretly obtained from prisons, and occasionally political prisoners are used.

India in this setting becomes a major proponent of "clean" energy, since it has a way to produce a lot of it, and becomes a leading energy exporter, creating another incentive for the govt not to discontinue the program.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
- Government approved systemic killing responsible for bringing basic amenity to society, with the general public being unaware of where the "clean energy" comes from
-Creation of energy via human sacrifice, facilitated by a machine created to kill a divine entity and harvest power from it, following E=MC^2.

Additional Notes: Let me know if the idea seems a bit too political or targeted. That's my main concern.
